stem.text: A particle moves along the polar curve \( r = 4 \sin{\left(\theta \right)} + 4 \) so that at time t its angle is \( \theta(t) = \frac{t^{2}}{2} \). Using a calculator, find the velocity vector of the particle at time \( t = 0.8 \). Show the setup, and give each component correct to three decimal places.

worked_solution.text: With \( x = r\cos\theta \) and \( y = r\sin\theta \), the position vector in terms of time is \( \left\langle x(t), y(t) \right\rangle = \left\langle \left(4 \sin{\left(\frac{t^{2}}{2} \right)} + 4\right) \cos{\left(\frac{t^{2}}{2} \right)},\ \left(4 \sin{\left(\frac{t^{2}}{2} \right)} + 4\right) \sin{\left(\frac{t^{2}}{2} \right)} \right\rangle \).
Differentiate each component and evaluate at \( t = 0.8 \) with the calculator in radian mode: \( x'(0.8) \approx 1.560 \) and \( y'(0.8) \approx 4.949 \).
So the velocity vector is \( v(0.8) \approx \left\langle 1.560,\ 4.949 \right\rangle \).

options.label: \( v(0.8) \approx \left\langle 0.056,\ 0.056 \right\rangle \)
options.derivation: both component derivatives evaluated with the calculator in degree mode

options.label: \( v(0.8) \approx \left\langle 4.949,\ 1.560 \right\rangle \)
options.derivation: the two components written in the wrong order, the y-component first

options.label: \( v(0.8) \approx \left\langle 3.038,\ 0.800 \right\rangle \)
options.derivation: the polar pair taken as the position, so the velocity is reported as dr/dt and dtheta/dt
